# Clipman

> Wayland-native clipboard history manager for GNOME on Linux, built with GTK 4 and libadwaita. Press Super+V to search, pin and paste from a local SQLite-backed history. No telemetry; detected secrets are removed from the history.

- [Project page](https://mohammedel-sayedahmed.github.io/clipman/)
- [Source](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/clipman)
- [Design workspace](https://mohammedel-sayedahmed.github.io/clipman/design/index.html)
- [Changelog](https://github.com/MohammedEl-sayedAhmed/clipman/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

## Overview

Clipman is a clipboard history manager for GNOME desktops running Wayland. Unlike X11-era tools that poll the clipboard or rely on root-window hacks, Clipman cooperates with the compositor: a GNOME Shell extension reports every copy to the daemon over D-Bus. On GNOME the extension is required, because GNOME does not offer the data-control protocol that `wl-paste --watch` needs. The daemon runs as a user systemd service when installed with `install.sh`, and is stateless beyond a single SQLite database under `~/.local/share/clipman/`.

## Architecture

Clipman is written in Python 3.10–3.12 and built on GTK 4 + libadwaita 1.5+. The repository ships two halves: a long-lived daemon (the `clipman/` Python package, entry point `clipman.py`) that watches clipboard selections, persists them in SQLite, and renders the popup UI on demand; and a GNOME Shell extension (`extension/extension.js`) that runs inside the compositor's gjs process and forwards `owner-changed` clipboard events to the daemon over D-Bus.

The daemon's UI layer is libadwaita-first:

- `clipman/window.py` builds an `Adw.ApplicationWindow` with an `Adw.HeaderBar` and a virtualized `Gtk.ListView` history list (lightweight bound rows, no per-row `Adw.ActionRow`) — the popup that opens on Super+V.
- `clipman/preferences.py` ships the settings surface as an `Adw.Dialog` with a left navigation sidebar and **six panes**: Appearance (theme + accent/font color pickers + opacity + font size), Privacy (start-in-incognito + sensitive-data auto-clear + purge-now), Shortcuts (toggle binding + paste mode), Storage (max entries + database location + backup/restore), Updates (opt-out daily check, see ADR 0007), and About.
- `clipman/snippets_dialog.py` wraps the reusable-snippet editor in an `Adw.NavigationSplitView` master-detail dialog with a searchable list on the left and an editor form on the right (template variables `${date}`, `${time}`, `${clipboard}` included).
- `clipman/edge_states.py` declares **20 `StateSpec` entries** — empty history, no search results, incognito paused, sensitive auto-cleared, first-run, extension missing, backup failed, and the other intentional edge moments — dispatched at render time by `render_edge_state` into one of `Adw.StatusPage`, `Adw.Banner`, or `Adw.AlertDialog`.
- `clipman/window.py` injects the Catppuccin Mocha (dark) and warm-stone (light) palettes as `@define-color` overrides of libadwaita's named colors (`@accent_color`, `@window_bg_color`, `@card_bg_color`, …) ahead of `clipman/style.css`, so every Adw widget picks up the theme without per-widget CSS rules.
- `clipman/_version.py` is a leaf module holding the single `__version__` string literal; `clipman/__init__.py` re-exports it so the public `clipman.__version__` API still works while submodules can import the constant without re-entering the package root (CodeQL `py/cyclic-import`).

The daemon exposes a session-bus D-Bus interface at `com.clipman.Daemon` (`/com/clipman/Daemon`) for the toggle keybinding and clipboard ingest; the extension owns `org.gnome.Shell.Extensions.clipman` for paste-keystroke and window-placement calls back into the compositor. All storage is local: no network calls (except the opt-out daily update check against `api.github.com/repos/.../releases/latest`), no telemetry, no analytics.

## Supported compositors

- GNOME Shell 45–51 (Mutter / Wayland) through the bundled Shell extension; the app baseline is Ubuntu 24.04+ with GNOME 46
- KDE Plasma and wlroots compositors (Sway, Hyprland) are not supported yet; issue #318 tracks it
- X11 sessions are intentionally unsupported; legacy tools cover that case

## Privacy and security

Clips that match a known secret shape (vendor API tokens, private keys, JSON Web Tokens, URLs with a password inside, labelled values such as `PASSWORD=…`, Authorization headers, Luhn-valid card numbers, TOTP seeds, and command lines that take a password) are masked and removed from the history after a configurable delay (default 30 seconds). A bare password with no label is not detected, and the system clipboard itself is not cleared (issues #313 and #314). Incognito mode records nothing. The SQLite file and its write-ahead-log sidecars are clamped to mode `0600` and the data directory to `0700` on every daemon start, repairing loose permissions in place; the threat model is documented at `docs/threat-model.md`. Image clips are stored as content-addressed PNGs under `~/.local/share/clipman/images/` and pruned with the parent entry.

## Features

- Substring search over text clips and snippets (SQL `LIKE` with escaped wildcards)
- Pinning to keep entries past the history-size cap
- Reusable snippets with template variables (`${date}`, `${time}`, `${clipboard}`)
- Catppuccin Mocha (dark) and a warm-stone light palette; respects system dark/light preference
- 225 translatable strings in `po/clipman.pot`; no translations yet, and contributions are welcome (issue #321)

## Distribution

Released under Apache-2.0. Packaged for Snap Store, PyPI (`pipx install --system-site-packages clipman-clipboard`; the flag is required because the GTK4/libadwaita `gi` bindings come from distro packages), AUR (`clipman-clipboard`), and as standalone `.deb` / `.rpm` artifacts attached to each GitHub release.
